doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Taking the piano chair with the Ichiban Octet, a bebop band
summary: A pianist swapped jobs with her; she decided to learn bebop before knocking it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: He came to me, he said, you know, um, “Maybe we [should] switch jobs.” And in those days there was a thing called “bebop,” it was already in Japan. And [grumbles], “Bebop, that‟s not music,” something like that. So, he was playing with a band called Ichiban Octet…
… group, and this was a bebop band.

So he really didn‟t want that. He wanted to play swing style piano. And so, he came to me, said, you know, “Maybe we switch the piano, you play there, and I play with this group.” And then I said, “Well, I don‟t know,” I mean…. But I thought, “I shouldn‟t knock something that I don‟t even know. I should learn, then knock!” [laughs]

So, okay, I took a job, I was the piano player with Ichiban Octet. This was the group that was playing in the Shinagawa depot. This was the first, this was predominantly black people. I think maybe it was a sergeants‟ club, I‟m not quite sure.
